RGlimpse2

RGlimpse2 runs GLIMPSE2 genotype imputation and phasing for low-coverage whole-genome sequencing from R. It builds and installs the pinned GLIMPSE2_chunk, GLIMPSE2_split_reference, GLIMPSE2_phase, and GLIMPSE2_ligate programs, then invokes one child executable per operation through direct processx argument vectors.

Installation

Install development builds from the RGenomicsETL R-universe:

install.packages(
  "RGlimpse2",
  repos = c(
    RGenomicsETL = "https://rgenomicsetl.r-universe.dev",
    CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)

Source installation requires GNU make, a C++17 compiler, and the Boost iostreams, program_options, and serialization libraries. Rtools45 ships these requirements for Windows. Linux distributions and Homebrew provide them as ordinary development packages.

Packaged genetic maps

GRCh37 and GRCh38 autosomal, X non-PAR, X PAR1, and X PAR2 maps are installed with the package. Minimal zero-recombination coordinate maps are also provided for Y non-PAR and mitochondrial sequence:

library(RGlimpse2)

rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh38", "22")
rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh38", "X", region = "par1")
rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh37", "Y")
rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh38", "Y")
rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh37", "chrM")
rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh38", "MT")
head(rglimpse2_genetic_maps())
Assembly Map Coordinates
GRCh37 Y non-PAR 2,649,521-59,034,049
GRCh38 Y non-PAR 2,781,480-56,887,902
GRCh37 mitochondrial (M, MT, chrM, or chrMT) 1-16,569
GRCh38 mitochondrial (M, MT, chrM, or chrMT) 1-16,569

The Y files are explicitly named chrY_nonpar.*.gmap.gz. The Y and mitochondrial files contain two anchors at 0 cM because GLIMPSE requires at least two map entries. The native conformance tests run small haploid BCF reference/target pairs through chunk, split-reference, phase, and ligate using Y, chrY, M, MT, chrM, and chrMT. This proves contig-label mechanics, not scientific calibration of Y or mitochondrial imputation.

One explicit operation at a time

Resolve the installed executables and run an operation with explicit inputs, outputs, interval, seed, and resources:

library(RGlimpse2)

executables <- rglimpse2_executables(phase_backend = "auto")
if (rglimpse2_is_error(executables)) {
  stop(executables@message)
}

genetic_map <- rglimpse2_genetic_map("GRCh38", "22")

chunks <- rglimpse2_chunk(
  input_sites = "/data/reference.sites.bcf",
  region = "chr22",
  output_chunks = "/work/chunks.chr22.txt",
  executable = executables@chunk,
  genetic_map = genetic_map,
  seed = 20260727L,
  threads = 2L
)

Direct BAM/CRAM phasing uses the same selected phase executable. The alignment index is supplied explicitly and must use an adjacent filename that HTSlib will discover:

imputed <- rglimpse2_phase_bam(
  input_bam = "/data/sample.bam",
  input_index = "/data/sample.bam.bai",
  reference_bin = "/reference/chr22_100000_5000000.bin",
  output_bcf = "/work/sample.chr22.01.bcf",
  executable = executables@phase,
  seed = 20260728L,
  sample_name = "sample",
  sample_ploidy = 2L
)

Several samples, including mixed haploid and diploid samples, can be passed to one native phase process without writing an intermediate likelihood file:

alignments <- data.frame(
  input_bam = c("/data/sample-male.bam", "/data/sample-female.bam"),
  input_index = c(
    "/data/sample-male.bam.bai",
    "/data/sample-female.bam.bai"
  ),
  sample_name = c("sample-male", "sample-female"),
  sample_ploidy = c(1L, 2L)
)

imputed_cohort <- rglimpse2_phase_bams(
  alignments = alignments,
  reference_bin = "/reference/chrX_3000000_7000000.bin",
  output_bcf = "/work/cohort.chrX.01.bcf",
  executable = executables@phase,
  seed = 20260728L
)

CRAM input additionally requires an explicit reference FASTA and its adjacent .fai. SNP likelihoods are called directly from the alignment by default; call_indels = TRUE enables the GLIMPSE2 indel calling model. Biallelic symbolic and other non-observable reference alleles remain in the haplotype scaffold with flat read likelihoods.

Set read_fraction = 0.25 and read_fraction_seed = 0L in either BAM/CRAM wrapper to deterministically subsample read-name templates at a 0.25 rate before pileup, without writing subsampled alignments. Realized depth varies with the available templates. The native options are --read-fraction and --read-fraction-seed. Selection uses the samtools HTSlib X31/Wang hash and low-24-bit threshold; mates sharing a name receive the same decision, and fractions with the same seed are nested. Existing mapping/base-quality filters and max_depth still apply. One retains every read without consuming random draws; zero retains none. The subsampling seed is independent of the imputation seed. Nonzero seeds use samtools’ srand()/rand() expansion on the same C runtime; seed zero gives cross-runtime read selection. The read fraction applies to every row in a multi-alignment call.

Set haplotype_samples = TRUE in any phase wrapper to retain and export the actual allele samples after rephasing in each main iteration. FORMAT/HS packs two allele bits per draw: bits 2*d and 2*d+1 are the first and second haplotypes for zero-based main iteration d. NMAIN gives the draw count (1–15); haploid second bits are zero. Dense retention costs four bytes per input site and sample, including chunk buffers, independently of the draw count within this bound. Export leaves the existing GT/DS/GP calculations and random-number sequence unchanged.

These samples preserve GLIMPSE2’s linked rephasing of alleles sampled from per-site imputation marginals. They are not sampled reference-copying paths or soft per-haplotype probabilities. INFO/HSC identifies the input/output chunk intervals; draw indices are local to that scope. Ligation preserves HSC and swaps both allele bits of every diploid draw when it swaps GT. It rejects HS chunks with different NMAIN counts or mixtures of chunks with and without samples. A consumer must retain scope and must not concatenate the same iteration index across independently sampled chunks into a global draw. HS ligation consumes GLIMPSE2 phase output, whose diploid GT is complete and phased. HS with missing or unphased diploid GT is outside this producer contract; haploid allele samples remain unchanged. The same ligater accepts ordinary diploid VCF/BCF chunks, including converted QUILT2 NIPT maternal/fetal samples and categorical multiallelic genotypes. Each input chunk supplies one local phase set per sample. Input PS annotations are rejected, and adjacent chunks on one contig must have strictly increasing first record positions and share identical ordered allele records. Nested chunk extents are unsupported and fail when the right chunk ends before the left chunk. FORMAT/PS records per-sample phase sets: missing or tied informative overlap starts a separate set, while haploid, missing and unphased genotypes have no PS. FORMAT/LIGATE_FLIP records applied pair swaps and INFO/LIGATE_CHUNK selects the original ordered input chunk for each complete output record. Consumers use this source to retain matching posterior evidence; GP/DS and biological parent-origin probabilities keep their original allele semantics. The native export option requires VCF/BCF and rejects checkpoint input/output.

The split-reference, phase, and ligate wrappers follow the same contract. They do not search PATH, overwrite an output, build shell command strings, or retain workflow state. Invalid calls signal typed rglimpse2_contract_violation conditions; expected operational failures are returned as typed S7 error values. Split-reference rejects unsplit records with more or fewer than two alleles in the requested input region before starting the native process; reference preparation owns deterministic multiallelic decomposition.

One htslib authority

The package does not vendor or discover another htslib. During configuration it requires:

Rduckhts::rduckhts_htslib_config(validate = TRUE)

Every executable is built with the returned headers and exact library contract. Runtime executable discovery revalidates the packaged build version against the htslib version supplied and loaded by Rduckhts.

Runtime phase dispatch

GLIMPSE2_phase is built as complete, process-isolated executables:

  • x86_64: scalar SIMDe, AVX2, and AVX-512F/BW/VL;
  • ARM: scalar SIMDe and NEON.

A baseline C probe checks CPU features and operating-system vector state before "auto" selects a binary. Explicit backend selection supports conformance and reproducibility testing without process-global dispatch state.

rglimpse2_simd_info()
scalar <- rglimpse2_executables(phase_backend = "scalar")

The native tests run all four packaged GLIMPSE2 programs against eight tiny vcfppR-generated and Rduckhts-indexed BCF reference/target pairs. They cover 1/chr1, Y/chrY, and M/MT/chrM/chrMT, including haploid Y and mitochondrial targets, and require identical fixed-seed phase records from every runtime-supported backend. No executable test doubles are used.

Building this fork

The upstream GLIMPSE2 tree remains the repository root. The R package is nested under RGlimpse2/:

make r-package-bootstrap
make r-package-check

Reference-panel copying evidence is an inference diagnostic. RGlimpse2 does not call it local ancestry; that claim requires a separately calibrated and validated decoder.
